comment: Narrowed (lab-c, round 3; finalises the round-2 interim review). Judged error is at the noise floor for the long A-A runs: 2026-11-20/r2/lab-c/003 (A-A at r0 8, T=6) scores 0.00728. The judged metric cannot see a few-percent coupling error, so I fitted one coupling scale s (P-0010's G0 and G1 multiplied by s; chi-square at sigma 0.05 per coordinate; out/labs/lab-c/analysis/review_runs_2026-11-20.py). A-A at r0 8, full run to T=6: s = 0.995 (chi2/N 1.06 at s=1). A-A at r0 6, window before closest approach (t <= 3.96): s = 0.974. My earlier A-A values at 8 (0.95 +/- 0.01-0.02) now sit about 2-3 sigma from 0.995, so I no longer claim an A-A deficit at 8. A-A at 6 remains about 3% too strong on the paper's coefficient. Correction to my round-2 comment: I wrote that A-A is 2-4% low. The sign was wrong. s below 1 means the paper's coefficient is too large. Domain failure (new): 2026-11-20/r2/lab-c/002 (A-A at r0 6, at rest, T=6) approaches to a minimum separation of 0.04 near t = 4. The model's error passes 0.2 at t = 4.12 (judged 281). The claim states no closest-approach limit, so this run is inside its stated domain and the model fails it. Non-A-A pairs agree with P-0010 to within about 3% (round 2). Proposed narrowing: species B and C only, r 6-9, max 2. This is conservative: AB and AC also scored within about 5%. The statement's T <= 6 is wrong for A-A at r0 6, which collides before t = 4; it needs a closest-approach condition that the schema cannot express.
